questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Location, Availability and Social life.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Both Heidelberg and the ESN did a good job of making sure that every exchange student was well informed. I personally only had problems, when it came to choosing courses.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Socialising, orientation and information regarding opportunities at Heidelberg University.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I was living in Im Neuenheimer Feld, which is the science related campus. Most of the housing is priced around 340 euro/month. The apartments come as both single, double and 4 WG.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There are 3 Mensa's in total, two located in Altstadt and one in Im Neuenheimer Feld. Every day a new "power meal" is available for 2,70 € and if the "power meal" doesn't suit your taste, you can always check out the buffet for 1 € / 100g.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I would recommend either single apartments or housing with 3+ roommates. The Neuenheimer campus is quite far away from the Altstadt (not geographically, but because the busses have poor routing).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I got a document from my host university with a step by step guide for registration, which made the registration process really easy and straight forward.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Step by step guide from host university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not a single course from the course list was held this years winter semester... I ended up with 0 out of 5 courses that i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just take it easy, don't stress too much. Remember you can always send a mail to the erasmus coordinator and they will help you out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was forced to take a Masters course, since only 8 english courses were available for Computer Science students. The level was definitely high, but i'm not sure if it was the language barrier, the professors or the teaching style that made it even more difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was pretty similar in terms of structure. I had both lectures and exercise classes, just like at UCPH. The biggest difference was the exams being hand written 90 minutes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Algorithms and Data Structures 2
2. Einführung in Software Engineering
3. Embedded Machine Learning
4. IT-Sicherheit 1
5. Programmierkurs

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can recommend Programmierkurs and einführung in software engineering. These are both very interesting courses and they go hand in hand really well.

Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Rundfunkbeitrag (8 euro/month).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Local transport is really expensive if you don't have the D-Ticket. Everything from the supermarket is cheap (compared to denmark) and the same goes for restaurants and bars.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Hochschulsport provide sport groups that you can join for free or very cheap. The only problem is that the amount of people who can join these groups is very limited.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Bouldering, tennis, football and calisthenics.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to other close cities, visit bar streets, board game nights and sleepovers.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I have already been to germany many times (since my grandparent's live there), so I was already very used to it.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the ESN events (local students also come to these sometimes) and sign up for the buddy program.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Paying with cash almost everywhere and some places not accepting credit card.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Friendly, outgoing and entertaining people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. don't go there if you are studying computer science.
2. check out private housing (if you are early you might find way better alternatives)
3. make sure you have a SEPA approved bank account (it is a lot less stressful when you don't have to worry about manual money transfers every month)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting out of my comfort zone, meeting people from all over the world and gaining friends for life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Navigating websites, using heico, moodle, müsli.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
